AI News Briefing — 5 Nov 2026

TOP STORY: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company, buying the Git tooling (Trees, Diffs, Code Storage) that already sits inside Codex. Source control and code review, not chat, is where coding agents get judged.

KEY UPDATES
1. Tencent launches Hy4 — frontier open-weight model with visual understanding and computer use; weights and system cards promised within days.
2. Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro — 2.8T-parameter MoE with 1M-token context, open on Hugging Face; vLLM shipped day-0 serving support.
3. Gemini 4 Carbon nearly ties Claude Opus 5.5 on the GDPx benchmark (10.9% vs 12%) at roughly a third of the cost per task: $16.29 vs $51.41.
4. IndiaAI shows EKA-1, a small low-cost sovereign model, plus Dhir at 22B; Sarvam's Prism coding model keeps appearing in Indian model trackers.
5. An OpenAI-assisted audit reports 948 previously unknown Linux kernel vulnerabilities, while CrowdStrike pushes kill switches for autonomous agent actions.

CONCEPT OF THE DAY — The Task, Not the Token: cost per completed job, not cost per million tokens, is now the number that decides model choice. A new paper reporting 36.7x savings from context compaction makes the same point.

Full briefing: https://dilip457.github.io/ai-news-daily/
